title: Why open markets matter for global food system resilience
gist: World Bank senior economist Alberto Portugal warns that rising oil and gas prices are again pushing up fertilizer costs, and uses the 2022-23 crisis to argue that export restrictions (covering 11% of global food trade in 2022 vs 3% pre-pandemic) amplified price volatility and hurt the poorest most. Fertilizer markets, being concentrated and natural-gas dependent, stayed tight longer than food trade, so keeping food and fertilizer markets open is key to resilience.

insights.claim: Higher oil and gas prices are again raising fertilizer cost concerns because natural gas is the critical input for ammonia, which is processed into urea, the world's most widely used nitrogen fertilizer.
